author: GamingBolt
description:
Depending on what you thought of previous  Monster Hunter Stories games, this one could be your favorite. If you liked what you had before and wanted a more refined and polished take on it, you’ll love this. If you were intrigued by the past games, but wanted something more narratively or technically ambitious, this is the game that’ll finally get through to you. 

But if the tedium and repetition of the past few games gave you pause, well, things could go either way with Stories 3. While it does make several attempts to mitigate the repetition, the jury is out on whether or not they’re enough; certainly this is something that will vary person to person, and where I still found many aspects of the game tiresome, you don’t necessarily have to.
title: Monster Hunter Stories 3: Twisted Reflection Review - The Final Verdict

author: GamingBolt
description:
World of Warcraft: Midnight is a brand new expansion for the storied MMORPG that picks up right where The War Within left off with its final patch: the Sunwell is under siege from Xal’atath and her Void forces, and it’s up to Lady Liadrin, Lor’themar, Arator, Turalyon, Alleria, and the player to once again save the world from this new existential threat. Along the way, there are plenty of activities to do, from diving into dungeons, spelunking into delves, or just becoming an interior decorator with the housing system.

The only real downsides for Midnight, aside from the fact that it’s the second part in a planned trilogy means that newcomers might be lost with its plot. While zones like Zul’Aman are fantastic, others, like Harandar, feel woefully disconnected, and often quite boring. However, the dungeons are still great, and while many classes have suffered from losing some abilities, the core gameplay continues to be excellent.
title: World of Warcraft Midnight Expansion Review - The Final Verdict

author: GamingBolt
description:
Requiem might just be the best take on Resident Evil's potent blend of survival horror and action, but that doesn't mean that future games should be content with what it is now. 

We think that the next mainline entry carries the potential to take things up a notch, and perhaps close out some very compelling story arcs whilst allowing more iconic characters their time to shine. To that end, we've put down a few thoughts on what the next big game can do to stand out, and make it an experience worthy of joining Requiem. Join us as we take you through what we think should, and perhaps might, happen with Resident Evil 10.
title: Resident Evil 10 - 5 MAJOR Things It Needs To Learn From Resident Evil Requiem

author: GamingBolt
description:
Co-op games have been one of the most popular genres in gaming, and that’s for good reason. There’s a lot of joy to be had when the fun stems not only from overcoming the obstacles that the devs have put, but also working together as a team and solving the problems of your own making. That element of chaos and the ability to create emergent narratives out of the same gameplay loop can be really addictive, but not a lot of games in the current market have been able to satisfy that itch for the long term. 

For most of us, Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2 was the game that defined this particular brand of co-op carnage last year. Players would fondly remember the familiar feeling of slashing through hordes of enemies, teammates going down at the worst possible moment, and clutching through crucial moments with nothing but a sliver of health left. And if you are looking for a new game to satisfy that very itch, look no further than John Carpenter’s Toxic Commando.
title: Loved Space Marine 2? Toxic Commando Could Be Your Next Co-op Obsession
